description:
Entries for several real space agencies appear under the 'Wikimedia Commons contributors' heading on /credits instead of under their own agency section heading.

Expected: Every image-provenance entry whose agency field names a real space agency should appear under that agency's section heading (CSA, CMSA, CNSA, ESA, ISRO, JAXA, NASA, Roscosmos, SpaceIL, UAESA/UAESA, USAF, USSR Post) rather than under Wikimedia Commons. The retrieval conduit (Commons) is never the section heading for a known agency.

Acceptance criteria:
- Entries with agency 'UAESA' must route to source-id 'uaesa' (the section exists in source-logos.json). Currently 'UAESA' as a string does not match agencyToSourceId — only 'MBRSC' and 'UAE Space Agency' do. [repo-data: static/data/source-logos.json has 'uaesa' as 'MBRSC / UAE Space Agency' (line 93); static/data/image-provenance.json has 12 wikimedia-commons entries with agency 'UAESA']
- Entries with agency 'CSA' (Canadian Space Agency) must route to source-id 'csa'. Currently 'CSA' does not match any pattern in agencyToSourceId, and entries with primary token 'CSA' (from 'CSA / NASA') fall through to Commons. [repo-data: static/data/source-logos.json has 'csa' as 'Canadian Space Agency' (line 122); image-provenance shows 'wikimedia-commons' entries with agency 'CSA / NASA']

Domain facts:
- CMSA (China Manned Space Agency), SpaceIL, USAF, and 'USSR Post' do NOT have entries in static/data/source-logos.json. Routing them out of Commons requires either: (a) adding new source-logos entries for these entities so a section exists, or (b) mapping them to existing sections (CMSA → CNSA; SpaceIL → new entry or private-operator; USAF → us-space-force or new entry; USSR Post → roscosmos). The maintainer must decide which.
- The comment on agencyToSourceId lines 153-155 explicitly documents the editorial rule: 'the upstream publisher (the agency that flew the hardware / produced the image) wins over the retrieval conduit'. The missing mappings violate this stated rule.
